description: Explicit student references, plus the attendee-collision family (mc-23..mc-33) that guards the preservation rule in both directions — mc-28..mc-34 added in Z0B-1r2 for segment classification, mc-35..mc-37 added in Z0B-1r3 for gap-punctuation segment splitting (D4) and the role-pattern name-plausibility filter (D3), mc-38..mc-40 added in Z0B-1r4 to prove the trigger-gap/plausibility guards (G1/G2/G3) did not cost the detections they bound. Plan §12/§15: the bar is 100% — any miss is a red build. Every name here is synthetic; no real student, family or staff member appears in this file.

cases.text: Camila Fuentes abrió la sesión y comentó que la estudiante Martina Rojas ha mejorado mucho en lenguaje este semestre.

cases.description: two students coordinated by y — AMENDED in Z0B-1r2: expectedPersonCount added and set to 2. Before segment classification the connector-merged span produced ONE [persona N] for two students (defect D2), which undercounted personCount and the §6 flag-density metric; both mentions were redacted either way, so the case passed while the count was wrong.
cases.text: Los estudiantes Matías y Tomás presentaron juntos el trabajo de ciencias y les fue muy bien.

cases.text: La compañera Josefa la ayudó a ponerse al día después de la licencia médica.

cases.text: El informe menciona a María José Aravena como uno de los casos prioritarios del ciclo.

cases.text: Camila Fuentes coordinó la entrevista con la Sra. Elena para el martes a primera hora.

cases.text: El alumno Cristóbal Vergara llegó atrasado dos veces. Hablamos con Cristóbal en la mañana y quedó claro. Cristóbal Vergara se comprometió a avisar si vuelve a pasar.

cases.text: Camila Fuentes y Rodrigo Pérez coincidieron en que el caso de Ignacia Lillo requiere derivación externa.

cases.description: attendee full name after a redacted collision — full coverage beats token contamination

cases.description: D1 — student stitched from TWO different attendees' tokens: given name from one, surname from the other. Coverage is per roster entry, never the union, so the whole span goes.
cases.text: La alumna Camila Pérez llegó tarde a la sesión y quedó fuera de la actividad inicial.

cases.description: D1 plus a later bare given name — contaminated by the cross-entry collision, so it redacts and reuses that student's number
cases.text: La alumna Camila Pérez entregó el informe atrasado. Más tarde Camila preguntó por la nota en la sala.

cases.description: two attendees coordinated by y — buildSpans bridges them into one span, and each segment is covered by its own roster entry, so nothing is redacted
cases.text: Camila Fuentes y Rodrigo Pérez firmaron el acta de la sesión antes de cerrar la reunión.

cases.description: mixed span — attendee and student inside one bridged span; segments act independently, so the attendee survives and the student is redacted
cases.text: Conversamos con Camila Fuentes y Martina sobre el plan de acompañamiento del curso.

cases.description: D2 — two students joined by a connector must be two people, not one; the connector text survives between the tokens
cases.text: En la presentación el alumno Matías y Tomás mostraron el mismo experimento de ciencias.

cases.description: attendee whose name carries internal connectors — the roster entry explains every token, so the surface survives intact
cases.text: La sesión la abrió María de los Ángeles con el equipo directivo del colegio.

cases.description: two students joined by a comma. AMENDED TWICE. Z0B-1r2 set expectedPersonCount to 1 and documented it as residual R3: segments split at connector TOKENS only, so the pair shared ONE [persona N] — an undercount of the §6 density metric. Z0B-1r3 (defect D4) closed that: segments now also split at gap punctuation, so the count is 2. Both mentions were redacted under either rule; the count is what moved, which is exactly how the undercount stayed invisible for a round.
cases.text: En el grupo de apoyo quedaron Martina Rojas, Benjamín Soto y otro más.

cases.description: D4 — three students in one comma list: a role-noun pair, a bare comma-joined pair, and a third behind a connector. Three person-references, three numbers; before the gap-punctuation split the comma pair collapsed into one persona and the comma itself was swallowed by the replacement.
cases.text: Asistieron la alumna Martina Rojas, Benjamín Soto y la niña Florencia.

cases.description: D4 across a sentence boundary — buildSpans merges adjacent name tokens whatever sits between them, so a name ending one sentence and a name opening the next arrived as one span. Two students, two numbers, and the period between them survives in the output.
cases.text: Hablamos de la estudiante Martina Rojas. Benjamín Soto llegó tarde a la sesión.

cases.description: D3 — a name lowercased by transcription, next to a role noun. This is the case the role-pattern layer's lowercase branch exists for, and it must survive the name-plausibility filter that stopped 'los alumnos trabajaron' from producing a person: 'benjamín' is not ordinary vocabulary and carries no verb, participle or adverb morphology, so it is uncertain — and uncertain redacts.
cases.text: El equipo comentó que el alumno benjamín no ha entregado la guía de lectura.

cases.description: G2 applied to the HONORIFIC layer must not throw its lowercase branch away. 'ignacio' after 'don' is not ordinary vocabulary and carries no verb, participle or adverb morphology, so it is name-plausible → uncertain → redacted. This is the honorific twin of mc-37, and the case that proves the r4 fix for 'La profesora terminaba…' did not buy precision with recall.
cases.text: Conversamos con don ignacio sobre el rendimiento de su hijo en matemática.

cases.description: Same guarantee for a school honorific and a lowercased staff name — the mc-09 construction with the capitalization Whisper drops. 'la profe marcela' must still redact after G2.
cases.text: La profe marcela comentó que el bloque colaborativo se le ocupa en temas administrativos.

cases.description: G3 — left-extension veto. The sentence-opening verb 'Quedaron' was being absorbed into the persona span ('[persona 1] y [persona 2] a cargo…'), destroying the verb and reporting a person span that started one token too far left. Both students must still be redacted whole, with two numbers, and the verb must survive in the output.
cases.text: Quedaron Martina Rojas y Benjamín Soto a cargo del mural de la entrada.
